newsitem.title: USA: Star-Kist to close plant, cut about 400 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Star-Kist to close plant, cut about 400 jobs.

text.p: Star-Kist Foods, a unit of H.J. Heinz Co., said on Tuesday it will close an Illinois pet food plant and cut about 400 jobs as it restructures the company's Heinz Pet Products division.
The move comes as part of a larger restructuring announced in March by Heinz, in which the food company said it will close or sell at least 25 plants and cut its work force by 2,500.
Under the plan, Star-Kist will close its Kankakee, Ill., dry pet food and treats plant and cut back its Topeka, Kan., dry pet food plant over the next 10 months.
All of the dry pet food production in Kankakee and most in Kansas will be moved to regional sites operated by other manufacturers closer to customer bases, the company said.
Pet treats manufactured in Kankakee will be moved to Topeka, the company said.

About 291 hourly and 57 salaried positions will be affected by the Kankakee closure and 30 hourly and 10 management jobs will be cut due to changes in Topeka and the company's Lawrence, Kansas operation.
The facilities were acquired by the company in 1995 from Quaker Oats Co.
Heinz's stock fell 37.5 cents to $45.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
